title: Have Questions About the 2026 Women’s Leadership Accelerator? Come to Ou...
Maternal Tdap vaccine: The evidence behind it and how to tell the story
description:
Pertussis (whooping cough) cases are on the rise, and infants remain the most vulnerable population. Tdap vaccination during pregnancy is one of the most effective tools we have to protect newborns before they are old enough to be vaccinated themselves. In this webinar, you will hear from two expert groups working at the forefront of vaccine communication and evidence translation.

The Vaccine Integrity Project will present their evidence review of the current data on Tdap safety and efficacy in pregnancy, and The Evidence Collective will share the most common questions they hear from communities both on- and offline and discuss practical strategies for addressing them effectively.

Moderator

Tara Haelle

AHCJ Health Beat Leader for Infectious Diseases and Medical StudiesTara Haelle is AHCJ’s health beat leader for infectious diseases and medical studies. She’s an independent science/health journalist, author, speaker, and photographer. Her work has appeared in the National Geographic, Scientific American, Texas Monthly, Science News, Medscape/WebMD, The New York Times, Wired, and O Magazine, among others. She specializes in public health and medical research, particularly vaccines, infectious disease, maternal and pediatric health, mental health, healthcare disparities, and misinformation. She also covers medical research conferences and edits Long COVID Connection on Medium. Haelle earned a master’s in photojournalism from the University of Texas at Austin, and her images have appeared in Texas Monthly, NPR, the, Chicago Sun-Times and elsewhere.

Bertha A. Hidalgo, Ph.D., MPH, FACE

Steering committee, The Evidence CollectiveDr. Bertha Hidalgo an Associate Professor with tenure in the Department of Epidemiology and Associate Dean for the Office of Access and Engagement at the UAB School of Public Health. She holds degrees from Stanford University, the University of Southern California and the University of Alabama at Birmingham. She leads research programs in genetic epidemiology and dissemination science.

Dr. Hidalgo has a highly productive record of peer-reviewed research in relevant research areas with publications as lead or co-lead author in high-impact journals including Nature, Scientific Reports, Diabetes, American Journal of Public Health, with over 100 publications in total as lead, co-author or senior author. She has attained research funding from the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, National Institutes of Health, the American Heart Association, and internal funding from UAB.

Dr. Hidalgo is the past chair of the Minority Affairs committee and current President of theAmerican College of Epidemiology, as well as a long-standing member on the NHLBI Board of External Experts. Dr. Hidalgo is also a recipient of the 2019 Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Early Career Achievement Award.

Elisabeth Marnik, Ph.D.

Executive director, The Evidence CollectiveDr. Elisabeth Adkins Marnik is a science communicator and immunologist working at the intersection of public trust, science, and public health. She earned her PhD in genetics and immunology from Tufts University.

Raised in a family that distrusted science and vaccines, Liz brings a personal understanding of hesitancy to her work. During the COVID-19 pandemic, she launched Science Whiz Liz to help the public navigate emerging health information, combining lived experience with scientific expertise. Liz now leads national efforts to translate evidence into clear, responsible, and empathetic public communication. She is an inaugural member of the National Academy of Medicine’s Action Collaborative on Building Trust in Health Science Through Community Partnership and Lived Experience and was named to Mainebiz’s 2025 40 Under 40 for her leadership in science education and public engagement.

Emily Senerth, M.S., MPH

Consultant researcher, Evidence FoundationEmily Senerth, M.S., MPH, is a Consultant Researcher for Evidence Foundation, a registered nonprofit organization based in Cleveland, Ohio whose mission is to support evidence-based health care through training, mentorship, education, and collaboration. Emily managed the development of a rapid systematic review and meta-analysis on the effectiveness and safety of Tdap vaccination during pregnancy commissioned by the Vaccine Integrity Project.

She has also led methodological reviews to investigate systematic review approaches and decision-making frameworks in environmental and occupational health, systematic reviews on the health effects of noise annoyance and the impact of socioeconomic status on faltering weight, and technical reviews to support the development of guideline recommendations on left atrial appendage occlusion, management of chronic venous disease, diagnosis and treatment of pediatric urinary tract infection, and lung cancer screening.

Rochelle Walensky, M.D., MPH

Professor of medicine, Harvard Medical SchoolMedical affairs adviser, Vaccine Integrity ProjectDr. Rochelle Walensky is a professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School and the medical affairs adviser for the Vaccine Integrity Project.

Dr. Walensky served as the 19th Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (2021-23), Professor of Medicine, Harvard Medical School (2012-2021), and Chief of the Division of Infectious Diseases, Massachusetts General Hospital (2017-2021). Dr. Walensky is a board-certified infectious disease clinician whose research and over 300 peer-reviewed publications has focused on infectious diseases and HIV/AIDS policy, including cost-effective strategies for HIV screening, treatment, and prevention, both in the U.S. and around the globe.

Dr. Walensky is a member of the American Academy of Physicians, National Academy of Medicine, and Council on Foreign Relations. She currently serves on the Board of Trustees at the Doris Duke Foundation and The Carter Center. She is also a founding member and Medical Affairs Advisor at the Vaccine Integrity Project, which is dedicated to providing trusted, science-based information for informed vaccine choices.

Dr. Walensky received her BA (Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1991) from Washington University in St. Louis; her MD from the Johns Hopkins School of Medicine (1995) and her MPH from the Harvard School of Public Health (Clinical Effectiveness, 2001). She completed her Internal Medicine residency at the Johns Hopkins Hospital (1995-1998) and her Infectious Disease fellowship at the Massachusetts General/Brigham and Women’s Hospital combined program (1998-2001).

title: Covering the Planet with the Tools That Tax It: AI for Climate, Science and Environmental Journalists
description:
Online
AI is both a tool transforming newsrooms and a story-shaping force in public life. How should journalists approach both with rigor?
Join us for a one-hour session with journalist and SF State University Professor Yumi Wilson. We'll talk about AI using the solutions journalism framework. We'll examine what AI actually does in newsrooms (response), what the evidence shows about its costs and benefits (evidence), what reporters are learning about its best uses (insight) and where AI falls short (limitations). You'll come away with a clearer understanding of how AI is shaping journalism worldwide and a practical prompting structure you can start using on the beat.

title: Find Your People: Engagement Strategies for Bringing Solutions Reporting to the Community
description:
Online
There is sometimes a gulf in reporting: Whether due to trust or access, the people most in need of the information can struggle to obtain it. SomeAdvancing Democracy granteeshave been addressing that in creative ways. You can learn from them at “Find your people: Engagement strategies for bringing solutions reporting to the community.”
We’ve got two sessions, May 7 and May 21, each featuring two different newsrooms finding success with including the public in solutions journalism. And we’ll help you build your own road map for meaningful engagement — not just adding to your reach, but building real relationships. You can sign up for one or both.
Part one — May 7: Gulf States Newsroom and Factchequeado share how they embedded community listening into their solutions reporting for the first time.
Part two — May 21: Crosswinds News and Texas Standard discuss building on prior solutions journalism training to deepen engagement on Native inclusion and adult education beats.

title: Health Journalism 2026
description:
Pack your bags for the City of Lakes! The Association of Health Care Journalists and the Center for Excellence in Health Care Journalism are thrilled to bring Health Journalism ’26 to Minneapolis from May 27–30. Expect four energizing days of immersive field trips, standout sessions, hands-on workshops and abundant opportunities to connect with colleagues from across the country.

“I’m excited that we’re returning to the middle of the country for our annual conference, after holding the last two in LA and New York,” said Gideon Gil, AHCJ board president. “This year, we’re starting the conference a day earlier, on a Wednesday, and ending on Saturday afternoon, to make it easier for attendees to stay through the last sessions before having to head home.”

At a moment when truth and accountability matter more than ever, we’ll bring together journalists, health care professionals, policymakers and industry experts for timely discussions. Be a part of the conversation (and pitch your ideas for sessions until Jan. 30, 2026) as we explore health care’s biggest challenges and examine emerging opportunities and solutions. As always, you’ll walk away with plenty of story ideas and new contacts.

This year’s conference will also feature the 22nd annual Awards for Excellence in Health Care Journalism, a celebration of the best work in health care reporting.

“AHCJ is committed to moving our conference around the U.S. to make it more accessible to our members,” said Kelsey Ryan, AHCJ executive director. “We’re excited to give a national lens to local places each year, and Minneapolis has a lot that everyone can learn from.”

Beyond the sessions, Minneapolis offers so much to see and do. Visit George Floyd Square at the intersection of 38th Street and Chicago Avenue, which will soon have a memorial. Listen to live music on First Avenue or wander through the legendary Minneapolis Sculpture Garden, home to Claes Oldenburg’s iconic “Spoonbridge and Cherry” sculpture. Dive into the city’s vibrant art scene at the Minneapolis Institute of Art, the Mill City Museum, the Weisman Art Museum and the Walker Art Center. And don’t forget to schedule a guided tour of Paisley Park, Prince’s former home and recording studio.

More details coming soon — but for now, save the dates, submit a session pitch and start making plans to be in Minneapolis!

title: Pre-conference Workshop: Field Safety Planning for Newsroom Leaders
description:
An INN Days 2026 pre-conference field safety workshop for newsroom leaders
As protests, upcoming elections, and a rapidly evolving political climate drive an increase in high-stakes newsworthy events, news leaders face growing pressure to safely manage and deploy staff and freelancers in the field. The frontlines for journalists are expanding, reaching beyond traditional danger zones into everyday beats and topics where journalists are increasingly finding themselves vulnerable.
Join us before INN Days on Tuesday, June 16 from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the conference venue for this hands-on session led by the Journalist Assistance Network (JAN).
Register
Register by June 2, 2026. Tickets are $49 and include a light breakfast and full lunch.
During the workshop, you’ll learn about best practices for deploying journalists safely in the field, with structured time to exchange strategies with fellow leaders and to work through a practical safety planning template covering what to do before, during, and after a safety incident in the field.

Ideal for: Executive Directors, Editors-in-Chief, Chief Operating Officers, Board Members, and other newsroom leaders responsible for staff safety and organizational policy
Key Takeaways: A draft field safety plan built collaboratively with experts, an understanding of gaps in your current protocols, and practical strategies for filling them
Format & Experience: Facilitated small group breakouts with safety experts, peer-to-peer exchange, and sharebacks; opt-in informal AMA with safety experts over lunch
Topics Covered: Data and device protection, legal protection, physical field safety, digital security, online harassment response, and psychosocial support
Schedule: This workshop will be from 9 to 2 p.m. on Tuesday, June 16. The INN Days conference will begin at 3:30 p.m.

Led by Journalist Assistance Network which includes Freedom of the Press Foundation, the Committee to Protect Journalists, the Reporter’s Committee for Freedom of the Press, PEN America, and the International Women’s Media Foundation.
This pre-conference workshop is separate from INN Days and requires its own registration. If you are planning to also attend INN Days, you must register separately here.
Register by June 2, 2026. Tickets are $49 and include a light breakfast and full lunch.
For questions, please contact gatherings@inn.org.

title: Pre-conference Workshop: Building A Board Development Plan
description:
An INN Days 2026 pre-conference board development workshop for executive directors
Boards are critical to nonprofit resilience Yet for many newsroom leaders, moving their board to the next level to meet their needs is a lot easier said than done. The challenge is finding the time and space to step back, assess where your board actually stands, and identify realistic next steps you can act on in the near term. This pre-conference workshop is designed to help you cut through that, offering a practical framework to build a clear path forward.
Join us before INN Days on Tuesday, June 16 from 11 to 2 p.m. at the conference venue for this hands-on session led by Arizona State University’s Knight Center for the Future of News.
Register
Register by June 2, 2026. Tickets are $29 and include lunch.
This 3-hour workshop will guide leaders through a research-based framework of the three phases of board development. You’ll be able to identify which stage your board is in, what common challenges exist at each phase, and identify concrete steps to move forward across a series of topics.

Ideal for: Executive Directors, Publishers, Board Chairs, and others responsible for managing or working with their organization’s board
Key Takeaways: Understanding of your board’s current stage of development, common challenges at each phase, tactics to work through them, and an actionable six-month plan
Format & Experience: Research-based presentations, small group discussions, and a guided near term action planning
Topics Covered: The three phases of board development, governance literacy and board composition, editorial independence and ethics, fiduciary oversight and fundraising, and enterprise risk management including safety, legal, financial, and AI-related risks
Schedule: This workshop will be from 11 to 2 p.m. on Tuesday, June 16. The INN Days conference will begin at 3:30 p.m.

This pre-conference workshop is separate from INN Days and requires its own registration. If you are planning to also attend INN Days, you must register separately here.
A condensed version of this session with limited capacity will be featured as part of the INN Days conference.
For questions, please contact gatherings@inn.org.

title: Pre-conference Workshop: The Rural Election Data Sprint
description:
An INN Days 2026 pre-conference workshop on turning election research and data into local reporting for Rural News Network (RNN) newsrooms
With the midterms just months away, many rural newsrooms are being asked to cover increasingly complex elections without the time, tools or staff to fully track the money, networks and influence shaping local races. This pre-conference session is designed to help close that gap—offering a hands-on, working lab where journalists can begin turning national data resources into local, actionable reporting.
Join us before INN Days on Tuesday, June 16 from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the conference venue for this hands-on session led by INN’s Rural News Network alongside INN members MuckRock’s Sunlight Research and OpenSecrets.
Register
Register by June 2, 2026. Tickets are $29 and include lunch.
In this interactive session, participants will work in small groups using tools from Sunlight Research and OpenSecrets to identify story angles, surface key data points and map out next steps for reporting. With guidance from experienced editors and data experts, attendees will move beyond theory and start building real election coverage grounded in their communities.

Ideal for: Reporters, editors, and data journalists at INN member rural newsrooms
Key Takeaways: Understanding of how Sunlight Research and OpenSecret’s resources can help you cover candidates and campaign finance, as well as potential story leads to jumpstart your elections coverage
Format & Experience: Walk-thrus of using candidate research and data tools, small group discussion, brainstorming activities to identify story leads and topics
Topics Covered: Campaign finance, outside money, candidate research and rural elections dynamics.
Schedule: This workshop will be from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Tuesday, June 16. The INN Days conference will begin at 3:30 p.m.

This pre-conference workshop is separate from INN Days and requires its own registration. If you are planning to also attend INN Days, you must register separately here.
Register by June 2, 2026. Tickets are $29 and include lunch.
For questions, please contact alana@inn.org.
